mcp.title: MCP server for AI agents
mcp.lede: The ADEXTO Model Context Protocol server allows automated agents to inspect bonding-curve markets and request purchases through an operator-controlled signing proxy. All analytical tools are public and unauthenticated, while purchase execution is restricted to a single authenticated tool governed by strict spending limits.

blocks.text: The ADEXTO MCP server is accessible at `https://adexto.xyz/api/mcp` over standard HTTP transports. Connecting an agent requires adding the endpoint to the client configuration, which enables market discovery without requiring account creation or authentication tokens for read operations.
The tools exposed by this endpoint are listed in the table below.

The interface separates market inspection from capital expenditure. All read-oriented tools are free, public, and operate without an account, an API key, or a funded balance. General requests to inspect market state or read trading histories proceed without credentials.
The single exception is the `pay_and_buy` tool, which is the only tool gated by authentication and capable of spending money. Requests to the remaining tools require no key or identity verification.

The agent does not hold private keys or control a spending wallet. When an agent decides to purchase tokens, it invokes the `pay_and_buy` tool, which requests that the server sign the transaction using the operator's private key stored on the server.
Because the signing key is maintained on the server, the agent decides to execute a purchase, but the server executes the purchase rather than the agent paying from its own funds.

The delivery address is never exposed or configurable by the agent because tokens always go directly to the signer address on the target curve. This prevents the agent from routing purchases to arbitrary recipient addresses.
Calls to the `pay_and_buy` tool require an `x-agent-key` header to authenticate against the server. If this header is missing or invalid, the server rejects the request immediately.

When executing a purchase, the server retrieves the HTTP 402 challenge from the gateway at `https://x402.adexto.xyz`. The server reads every term from the challenge response and compares it against hard-coded limits before signing the payment.

Capital risk is bounded along two distinct dimensions. The per-purchase cap bounds the size of any single transaction, while the per-hour call cap bounds invocation frequency rather than transaction size.
If any payment parameter returned in the gateway HTTP 402 challenge exceeds the hard-coded limits, or if the hourly call cap is reached, the server rejects the call before signing or spending funds.

trading.title: Trading a market
trading.lede: The ADEXTO bonding curve operates as a permanent trading venue that prices tokens against a virtual native reserve using a constant-product invariant. Because the protocol contains no graduation step or migration routine, token purchases and sales execute directly against the curve contract throughout the token lifecycle.

sections.heading: Constant Product Invariant and Permanent Curve Liquidity

blocks.text: The curve manages token pricing through a constant-product invariant evaluated against a virtual native currency reserve. This mechanism provides continuous on-chain pricing across trades, while each transaction incurs price impact dictated by the current reserve depth.

Many conventional launchpad models establish an arbitrary graduation target that halts trading and moves liquidity into an external automated market maker. The ADEXTO curve excludes graduation steps and migration routines entirely, leaving the curve contract as the permanent trading venue for the asset.
Because the protocol has no migration function, reserve assets remain permanently locked inside the curve contract, but liquidity is never consolidated automatically into third-party pools.

Selling tokens follows the exact same contract path as purchasing them. To exit a position, a user first grants an allowance to the curve contract through a standard ERC-20 approval transaction, and then executes the sell function against the identical curve contract.

Every trade execution function requires a slippage limit such as `minTokensOut` alongside an execution `deadline` timestamp. These parameters revert the transaction if price impact breaches the user's limit or if network congestion delays inclusion past the specified block timestamp.

items: The seller issues an ERC-20 approval granting the curve contract permission to transfer the specified token quantity.
The seller executes the sell transaction against the curve contract, supplying a minimum output threshold to enforce slippage protection.
The curve contract verifies the Unix timestamp deadline to ensure that delayed transactions revert rather than executing against stale reserve balances.

blocks.text: Integrators should read the swap fee from the curve with the `totalFeeBps` view rather than summing fee legs off-chain. Every leg is immutable per curve, but the generations differ: on the 0.11.0 curves the `protocolBps` leg of 10 basis points is added on top of the configured total, while on ADEXTO v1 curves it is carved out of it.

Fees never change after launch, and the launch window limits how much a wallet may hold without changing any fee. The contract enforces an absolute ceiling where `maxTotalBps` is 500 basis points, and `totalFeeBps` returns the total a trader pays on that curve.
Summing the configured legs off-chain gives the wrong total on a 0.11.0 curve, where the protocol leg is added on top; `totalFeeBps` is correct for both generations.

sections.heading: Token Standard and External AMM Coexistence

blocks.text: The token deployed by the curve factory is a standard ERC-20 implementation without owner privileges, pause switches, or address blacklists. The contract executes transfers according to the standard token specification without administrative overrides.

Because the token contract lacks restrictive controls, any market participant can permissionlessly pair the token with other assets on an external AMM. A secondary external market can exist concurrently alongside the bonding curve, enabling independent price discovery across multiple venues.
The protocol does not monitor or maintain liquidity on third-party venues, which means price levels and pool depths on external AMMs can diverge from the bonding curve.

The protocol guarantee is strictly defined and narrower than a guarantee of a single exclusive market. ADEXTO guarantees that its contracts will never migrate reserves to external pools and that no party can withdraw the curve contract's native assets.

The protocol does not guarantee that token trading will remain confined to the curve venue. Because anyone can launch third-party liquidity pools permissionlessly, the curve guarantees the permanence and custody of its own reserves rather than exclusive market concentration.

items: The protocol contracts contain no instructions to transfer or migrate curve liquidity to external pools.
No contract owner, factory administrator, or privileged account possesses the authority to drain curve reserves.
The protocol does not prevent third parties from establishing independent secondary markets on external venues.

fees.title: Fees
fees.lede: Every swap on an ADEXTO curve pays four fee legs: creator, depth, buyback and protocol. Each rate is fixed when the market is created, and each balance can only go to a destination fixed at the same moment. Where the protocol leg sits depends on the factory generation that created the market.

blocks.text: Each trade on an ADEXTO bonding curve pays four fee legs: the creator fee, the depth fee, the buyback fee, and the protocol fee. The creator chooses the total and the creator and buyback shares at launch. Depth is whatever remains, and the protocol leg is a 10 bps constant set by the factory.
On the markets listed today, all created by the 0.11.0 factories, `depthFeeBps` is 15 bps and `buybackBps` is 5 bps. Read `totalFeeBps` on a curve for the exact figure a trade pays there.

On the ADEXTO v1 factory (1.0.0), which every new launch uses, the 10 bps protocol leg is carved out of the configured total. A trader pays exactly the total the creator set, and that total cannot exceed the `maxTotalBps` limit of 500 bps.

On the 0.11.0 factory, which created every market listed today, the protocol leg is added on top of the configured total. A market configured at 30 bps charges a trader 40 bps, and the configured total plus the protocol leg cannot exceed 500 bps.
A creator cannot reduce or waive the 10 bps protocol leg in either generation. It is a constant in the factory and an immutable value in each curve.

All fee parameters are assigned during curve deployment, and the contracts provide no setter functions to alter them. Neither the market creator nor the factory contract can adjust fee rates after initialization.

Curves created by factories older than 0.11.0 pay no protocol fee at all. Because fee parameters are immutable once deployed, those markets never will, and a 0.11.0 market keeps its protocol leg on top of the configured total permanently.

The contract implements `claimProtocolFees` and `claimCreatorFees` to distribute accrued balances. Any caller can trigger these functions because the recipient destinations are assigned during curve construction and cannot be modified.
Because payout destinations are immutable, permissionless execution allows balances to be collected without requiring privileged transactions or risking asset redirection.

The buyback function can be called by any account to acquire tokens using accumulated buyback reserves. Each invocation is capped per call to restrict the volume executed in a single transaction, and curves from the ADEXTO v1 factory also wait one hour between calls.

Tokens purchased through buyback transactions are burned immediately by the curve contract. This mechanism contracts the circulating token supply without distributing assets to an external caller or designated wallet.
Buyback calls burn purchased tokens directly within the execution logic, preventing any party from obtaining custody of the acquired assets.

chains.title: Chains and deployments
chains.lede: The ADEXTO v1 factory (version 1.0.0) runs on six EVM mainnets. Each deployment contains exactly 21806 bytes of runtime bytecode with an identical keccak256 hash across all six networks.

blocks.text: The protocol maintains deployments on 0G Mainnet, Base Mainnet, Arbitrum One, Monad Mainnet, Robinhood Chain and Arc. Each network executes factory version 1.0.0.
A factory address is not unique to one mainnet: Robinhood Chain and Arc use the same one. Integrations must verify the chain ID alongside the contract address before submitting transactions.

The deployed factory contracts share the exact keccak256 hash of `0x1ca02ca53a3b2a2082f9e5dab6924e1339110e3037608f750981699678881fd4` across all six mainnets. This confirms that the deployed instruction sets are identical across all targets.

Byte-identical runtime bytecode is not automatic across separate chain deployments. In Solidity, immutable values are not stored in contract storage slots; the constructor inlines these constants directly into the deployed runtime opcode stream.

Because immutable variables sit directly inside the runtime code, the runtime bytecode hashes match only because the identical protocol treasury address was supplied at deployment time on every chain. Any change to constructor parameters would alter the opcode payload and yield a different hash.

A locally compiled contract artifact does not produce the runtime bytecode hash observed on-chain. In the compiler output, immutable variable positions contain unassigned zero-value placeholders that are only populated when constructor execution completes.

This mismatch between local compilation outputs and on-chain bytecode is expected compiler behavior rather than a deployment flaw. Verifiers must compare extracted on-chain runtime bytecode against deployed code on other chains rather than against raw local compilation artifacts.

Standard deployments derive contract addresses using the `CREATE` opcode, which computes addresses from the deployer account address and its current transaction nonce. When a deployer maintains equivalent nonce ordering across multiple networks, an identical address can appear on more than one chain.

Because `CREATE` address calculation is agnostic to the target network, callers must always confirm the active chain ID. Matching contract addresses on different chains do not guarantee identical state or administrative ownership.

x402.title: Buying from another chain with x402
x402.lede: The ADEXTO x402 gateway allows buyers to purchase bonding-curve tokens across chains by submitting an EIP-3009 transfer authorization in response to an HTTP 402 challenge. The operator executes delivery on the target chain before collecting payment on the source chain, though the two transactions remain non-atomic.

sections.heading: The HTTP 402 Challenge and Quote Negotiation

blocks.text: An unpaid GET request sent to a purchase endpoint at the gateway, such as `https://x402.adexto.xyz/v1/x402/buy/zeebo`, returns an HTTP status of 402 Payment Required with a `WWW-Authenticate` header set to `x402 realm="adexto-buy-zeebo"`.

The response payload provides an `accepts` array that details payment parameters, including the required payment asset contract at `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913` on Base, the payee address `0x24268Fffc119ec5550F68e80D94476fD64daE967`, the maximum amount `100000`, and a `maxTimeoutSeconds` value of `300`. It also returns a quote carrying the curve parameter `minTokensOut`, matching the fields `["symbol", "token", "curve", "chainId", "chain", "payWith", "deliver", "rate", "inventory"]`.

To fulfill the payment requirement, the caller signs an EIP-3009 `TransferWithAuthorization` message. Because EIP-3009 uses EIP-712 typed data signatures, the buyer does not need to pay native gas fees on the payment chain or submit a separate token allowance transaction.

The gateway verifies the signature against the EIP-712 domain read directly from the USDC contract on-chain rather than reading the domain from the client HTTP request. This on-chain domain lookup ensures that domain attributes such as the verifying contract address and chain identifier cannot be spoofed by a caller.

The operator executes delivery on the target chain before broadcasting the payment authorization on the payment chain. For a purchase of `ZEEBO` on 0G Mainnet with chain ID `16661`, the operator submits a buy transaction directly to the bonding curve at `0xBCdDE7f6071da3fc33f959F6A8B919dd921af49A`, which mints or transfers the purchased tokens directly to the buyer's destination address.

The operator submits the EIP-3009 authorization to collect funds only after the target curve delivery transaction confirms. If the fill transaction on the target chain fails or reverts, the operator absorbs the gas loss and never broadcasts the payment authorization, preventing the buyer from being charged for an unfulfilled order. When execution succeeds, the HTTP response body returns the transaction hashes for both the delivery leg and the payment leg.

The delivery transaction and the payment authorization execute as two separate operations across distinct blockchains and are not atomic. The buyer depends on the operator to broadcast the curve purchase after receiving the signed authorization.

Operator liquidity on destination chains is finite. If the operator lacks sufficient inventory or funds to fulfill the order on the destination curve, the gateway answers with an HTTP status of 503 before storing, processing, or broadcasting the buyer's payment authorization.
The cross-chain delivery and payment legs are not atomic. If operator liquidity is insufficient, the endpoint returns an HTTP 503 response before touching any authorization payload.

When the target market resides on the same network as the payment token, no funds cross between chains. For example, purchasing `BLOOP` (token contract `0xC980987be6fF737E55e65Bb67Cdd2F231Aa0fa6B`, curve contract `0xdEC37908476Ba7C159fBd28C687b7dE43079E4E4`) on Base Mainnet with chain ID `8453` using Base USDC executes entirely within Base Mainnet.

The gateway handles same-chain purchases through the exact same code path as cross-chain trades, executing the curve delivery first and charging the EIP-3009 authorization second. The markets table details all available bonding curves across supported networks.

agent-identity.title: Agent identity (ERC-8004)
agent-identity.lede: ADEXTO integrates the Identity Registry from the ERC-8004 specification to bind agent identifiers to bonding curves at launch. The protocol checks agent ownership during market deployment but excludes reputation tracking, validation registries, and interface detection.

blocks.text: The ERC-8004 draft specification outlines three independent registries: Identity, Reputation, and Validation. The ADEXTO factory and bonding curve contracts interact solely with the Identity Registry.
Neither the factory nor the bonding curves implement `supportsInterface`, and the protocol makes no calls to the Reputation Registry or the Validation Registry.
Because the underlying specification remains in Draft status, protocol integration is restricted to verifying agent ownership during deployment.
An agent identifier is bound to a market only during contract creation, and the registration of that agent is an external prerequisite.
The creator must register the agent on the Identity Registry in an independent transaction before deploying the market.

When a creator supplies an agent identifier at launch, the factory invokes `ownerOf` on the Identity Registry. If the caller does not match the owner returned by the registry, the factory reverts the transaction.

sections.heading: Identifier Semantics and the agentBound Flag

blocks.text: The contracts track whether an agent is attached using an explicit `agentBound` boolean flag rather than evaluating whether the agent identifier is non-zero.

In the Identity Registry, token identifier 0 represents a real agent with a legitimate owner. Inspecting the numeric identifier instead of `agentBound` would incorrectly treat token 0 as an unassigned slot.

items: The `agentBound` storage variable records whether an agent was associated with the curve at creation time.
The numeric `agentId` field stores the token identifier, which may validly be 0.

blocks.text: An agent identifier has no meaning without its specific chain. Every network hosts an independent registry deployment that maintains its own isolated storage and token sequence.

An identifier on one chain does not correspond to the same agent or owner on another chain. The factory contract on each network queries only the local Identity Registry deployed on that same network.
Each factory listed above executes calls against the local Identity Registry for its network and maintains no cross-chain registry synchronization.

The Identity Registry is deployed as an upgradeable proxy owned and controlled by an external third party. ADEXTO holds no administrative keys or governance authority over the registry implementation.

Because the Identity Registry is an externally owned upgradeable proxy and ERC-8004 is a Draft specification, registry behaviour, internal functions, and storage structures can change without notification or involvement from ADEXTO.

items: Logic upgrades deployed by the proxy owner can modify how `ownerOf` executes without altering factory bytecode.
Agent registration logic and metadata storage are managed entirely by the external proxy.
Reputation scoring and third-party validation registries from ERC-8004 are not queried, stored, or verified by any ADEXTO contract.

data.title: Reading market data
data.lede: ADEXTO resolves market state through on-chain factory contracts as the primary authority, while using chain-specific indexing pipelines for historical log aggregation. The on-chain registry determines market existence directly so that indexing latency does not cause newly launched markets to appear nonexistent.

sections.heading: Factory Registry Authority and Indexer Latency

blocks.text: The factory contract on each chain serves as the sole authoritative registry for market existence. While auxiliary indexers ingest logs asynchronously, direct state reads from the factory contract alone decide whether a bonding-curve market exists at any given block.

An indexer necessarily operates behind the current chain tip. If a caller queries an indexer immediately after a market launch transaction succeeds, an indexer that has not yet processed the transaction block would report that the market does not exist. Indexers operate strictly as an additive caching layer for trade history, while canonical verification requires querying the factory directly.
A market exists on-chain as soon as its creation transaction confirms on the factory contract, regardless of the processing delay in downstream indexing services.
Read paths differ across the supported networks due to varying external infrastructure availability on each blockchain.

items: Base Mainnet and Arbitrum One use hosted subgraphs to index contract events.
Monad Mainnet, Robinhood Chain and Arc use an Envio HyperIndex deployment for log indexing and queries.
0G Mainnet reads event logs directly from the node RPC endpoint at `https://evmrpc.0g.ai` because The Graph does not offer indexing support for chain ID 16661.

blocks.text: Direct RPC log scanning removes dependency on third-party indexers on 0G Mainnet, but it requires clients to handle RPC query boundaries directly.
Market data on Monad Mainnet (chain ID 143) is indexed through Envio HyperIndex. The service is publicly queryable without requiring user account registration or an access key.

Read-only access to the Envio indexer is enforced through PostgreSQL database role permissions. Because this read-only role restricts schema access, the exposed public schema contains no mutation root, preventing unauthorized state modification while serving public historical queries.

The Envio indexer has no lookback window, and neither do the subgraphs on Base and Arbitrum One or the per-market index that covers every market, including those on 0G. Only the live log scan that supplies the newest fills is bounded by RPC block span limits, and the `trade_history` tool reads these sources in that order.

sections.heading: Direct RPC Log Scanning and Measured Limits

blocks.text: Because 0G Mainnet lacks third-party indexing, market trade history is gathered by scanning event logs directly via `eth_getLogs` calls against `https://evmrpc.0g.ai`. This structure functions without dedicated indexing servers, but it is constrained by RPC node rate and range parameters.

Node providers place strict limitations on the maximum block range and the number of event logs returned per `eth_getLogs` request. ADEXTO measures these block range limits dynamically rather than relying on assumed values, because infrastructure providers routinely tighten filter boundaries without prior notice.

When an answer cannot be shown to reach the launch block of a market, for example while that market's index is still catching up, the response says so and names the blocks not read yet, rather than presenting the partial record as a complete history.

All six networks run factory version 1.0.0. The deployed bytecode is identical across each chain, measuring 21806 bytes with the keccak hash `0x1ca02ca53a3b2a2082f9e5dab6924e1339110e3037608f750981699678881fd4`.

security.title: Security and guarantees
security.lede: The ADEXTO smart contracts deploy immutable bonding curves without administrative control, upgradability proxies, or balance extraction functions. While these mechanisms eliminate discretionary intervention, no security firm has reviewed the codebase.

sections.heading: Immutable Fee Rates and Launch Architecture

blocks.text: The protocol enforces fixed fee parameters across its contracts. The protocol fee is set to 10 bps and the maximum total fee is bounded at 500 bps. For 180 seconds after launch, no wallet may hold more than 1% of supply.

Nothing on the launch path possesses an owner, an administrator, or a setter function. This design guarantees that fee rates and launch configurations cannot be modified after deployment, but it also prevents any adjustment to these settings if market requirements change.

sections.heading: Native Asset Flow and Absence of Extraction Functions

blocks.text: There is no withdraw, sweep, rescue, or drain function anywhere in the curve contracts. Native cryptocurrency can leave a curve contract through only two paths: a seller's payout disbursed upon selling tokens back to the curve, or an accrued fee claim routed to an address fixed at construction.
Because the curve contracts lack any recovery or drain mechanism, native currency or tokens sent to a contract by mistake cannot be recovered.

sections.heading: Frozen Bytecode and Absence of Upgrade Paths

blocks.text: The protocol deploys without proxies, fallback upgrade patterns, or delegatecall modifications. Across all deployed chains, the factory contract bytecode comprises 21806 bytes with a keccak hash of 0x1ca02ca53a3b2a2082f9e5dab6924e1339110e3037608f750981699678881fd4.

Because deployed bytecode is completely frozen, an unauthorized entity cannot alter contract rules. However, this immutability also means that a future bug fix cannot reach a market that already exists; resolving an issue requires deploying a completely new market instance.

The repository evaluates contracts against 8 analyser engines tested at commit c14c62446e4ee4ce0e56a9e31d1edeb0603dbb6a. The testing suite applies static analysers, compiler linters, fuzzing suites, and invariant property checks.
While automated analysers check known structural vulnerabilities and verify specific assertions, they cannot evaluate high-level economic designs or unforeseen edge conditions.

sections.heading: Independent Review Status and Vulnerability Disclosure

blocks.text: No security firm has reviewed the contracts. Published analyser output provides insight into automated test results, but it is not a substitute for an external manual audit.
Researchers and developers who discover potential vulnerabilities must report their findings through GitHub private vulnerability reporting.
Participants interact directly with autonomous smart contracts that operate without third-party audit verification or administrative override capabilities.

launch.title: Launch a market
launch.lede: The ADEXTO factory deploys a bonding-curve market in a single transaction without accepting an initial native liquidity deposit. The entire token supply transfers into the curve at creation, locking the symbol permanently while enforcing a temporary per-transaction purchase cap.

blocks.text: The factory initializes a new bonding-curve market through the `deployTrinity` function in a single transaction. The `deployTrinity` function is non-payable, which prevents the creator from depositing native currency at creation time.
Because the function cannot receive native funds, the market establishes its native side entirely with virtual liquidity rather than real pooled deposits.
The `deployTrinity` entry point does not accept native currency, so market creators cannot seed initial liquidity deposits during deployment.
During market deployment, 100% of the token supply transfers directly into the bonding curve. The market creator retains no initial token allocation and receives no creator reserves.
Once the transfer completes, the factory checks an explicit assertion that its own balance of the token is zero. This check verifies that the factory has not retained any portion of the supply.

For `antiSnipeWindowSeconds` (180 seconds) after launch, the token refuses any transfer that would leave the receiving wallet holding more than `antiSnipeMaxWalletBps` (100 bps, 1%) of supply. The limit is on the wallet balance, not on a single transaction, so splitting a purchase across many transactions does not get around it.

Three recipients are exempt: the curve, so holders can sell during the window; address(0), so buyback burns are never blocked; and the factory, which receives the mint and moves the whole supply into the curve in the launch transaction.

The window is measured with block.timestamp, so it lasts 180 seconds on every chain, and it ends by itself: there is no switch to extend it. Markets from the 0.11.0 factories used an earlier form, a 1% cap per transfer for their first 5 blocks.
A market claims its token ticker on-chain through the `symbolRegistry` contract during initialization. The symbol is claimed permanently on that specific chain.
The `symbolRegistry` contract does not contain a release function, so a registered ticker cannot be removed, reallocated, or repurposed after deployment.
The deployment transaction allows an optional binding to an ERC-8004 agent identifier, but this configuration is disabled by default. The deployment process does not register an agent.
If an agent identifier is specified, the factory only verifies that the caller owns the identifier by querying `ownerOf` on the target contract.
The factory does not perform agent registration during market creation; it solely verifies ownership of an existing identifier via `ownerOf`.

The Studio has two modes and opens in Express. Express asks for a name, a ticker and an image, and launches through the same `deployTrinity` call with the settings below, simulated first. Advanced is the five-step form, at `/studio?mode=advanced`. Every setting stays editable in Advanced before launch, and switching modes keeps what was typed.

items: Chain: the one picked in Express, or else the first chain that can launch, in the order Monad, Arbitrum, Robinhood Chain, Base, Arc, 0G.
Fee: the Standard tier, 1.00% per trade, of which 0.70% goes to the creator, 0.10% stays in the curve as depth, 0.10% funds the buyback and 0.10% is the protocol leg.
Supply: 1,000,000,000 tokens, all of them in the curve and none to the creator.
Market agent: a neutral persona that answers questions about the market. No ERC-8004 identity is bound.
Wallet prompts: one free signature that proves control of the address, then the launch transaction, which costs gas and takes no deposit.

blocks.text: A link of the form `/studio?mode=express&name=…&symbol=…&chain=…` opens Express with those fields filled. The link launches nothing by itself; whoever opens it signs with their own wallet.
The factory contract is deployed across six EVM mainnets using identical bytecode. The deployed factory addresses and chain identifiers are provided in the table below.

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.lede: Connect a wallet, buy a token on its market page, and launch a market of your own from the Studio.

blocks.text: A wallet that runs in your browser, such as MetaMask, Rabby or Coinbase Wallet, or a mobile wallet that connects through WalletConnect. ADEXTO never asks for your seed phrase or private key: you sign every launch, trade, stake and claim in your own wallet.
A little of the chain's own asset to pay gas: MON on Monad, ETH on Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain and Base, USDC on Arc, and 0G on 0G. To move funds between chains, use the Cross-chain tab on `/swap`.
Launches and trades are real transactions on mainnet. Check the network and the amount in your wallet before you confirm.

items: Open `/explorer` and pick a market. Every row shows its chain, and the same ticker on another chain is a separate market with its own price.
On the market page, connect your wallet. If the wallet is on another network, the app asks it to switch, and to add the network if the wallet does not have it yet.
In the swap card, choose Buy and enter an amount in the chain's own asset. Check `Minimum received` and `Price impact` before you sign.
Confirm in your wallet. If the price moves past your slippage limit before the trade is mined, the trade reverts instead of filling at a worse price.

blocks.text: Selling works the same way from the Sell side of the card. A sale first asks for an approval of the exact amount, when the curve does not already have one, and then sends the sale (`Approve & sell`).

sections.heading: Launch a market of your own

items: Open `/studio`. It starts in Express mode, which asks for a name, a ticker, an optional one-line description, an image and one chain.
Read `Settings used`: a 1.00% fee on every trade, of which 0.70% goes to you, and a supply of 1,000,000,000 tokens, all of them in the curve and none to you.
Read the cost card. The launch accepts no deposit, so you pay gas only, and you receive no tokens.
Accept the terms and press the launch button. Your wallet asks twice: first a free signature that proves you control the address, then the launch transaction, which costs gas.

blocks.text: When the transaction confirms, the Studio links to your market's page and to Creator earnings, where your share of every trade adds up until you claim it.
Each of these pages takes a few minutes to read.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.lede: Short definitions of the words used across ADEXTO and these docs.

items: Market: one token and its bonding curve on one chain. The same ticker on two chains is two markets, each with its own supply and price, and nothing is bridged between them.

Bonding curve: the contract that holds a market's tokens and its native reserve, and prices every trade from them with a constant-product formula over a virtual native reserve. You always trade against it, never against another person's order.
Virtual reserve: a native amount that the curve counts in its formula but never holds. It sets the opening price without anyone depositing liquidity.
Opening market cap: the market cap at launch. The Studio sets it to about $4,000 on every chain, using the native price at the time of the launch.
Market cap: the price times the total supply. Because the whole supply starts in the curve, the chart's MCAP view is the same as the fully diluted value.
Price impact: how far your own trade moves the price. A larger trade against a smaller reserve moves it more.
Slippage limit: the worst result you accept. A trade carries a minimum output and reverts if it cannot meet it.
Deadline: the time after which a signed trade can no longer execute. The swap card sets it to 600 seconds.
Fee: the percentage of every trade that the curve keeps back, fixed at launch. It is split into four parts.
Creator part: the creator's share of every trade. It accrues in the curve, in the chain's native asset, and is claimed later.
Depth: the part that stays in the curve's reserve, so the market gets deeper as it trades.
Buyback: the part that is set aside to buy the token back from the curve and burn it. Anyone can trigger a buyback, at most once an hour, and each one spends at most 1% of the curve's native reserve.
Protocol part: 0.10% of every trade for ADEXTO. On markets from the current factory it sits inside the total; on the six earlier markets it is added on top.
Claim: the transaction that pays accrued fees to their recipient. Anyone can send it, and the money still goes to the recipient fixed at launch.
Basis point (bps): one hundredth of a percent. 100 bps is 1%.
Ticker: the market's symbol, 2 to 12 letters or digits. It is permanent on its chain and taken regardless of letter case, and some tickers are reserved.
Launch window: the first 180 seconds of a market from the current factory, when no wallet may hold more than 1% of the supply. The curve is exempt, so selling still works.
Express and Advanced: the two Studio modes. Express asks for a name, a ticker and an image; Advanced is the five-step form with every option.
Launch attestation: the free message you sign before the launch transaction. It states your address, the ticker, a timestamp and the version of the terms you accept.
Clean-launch proof: a set of checks read from chain that shows how a launch went, such as where the supply went and whether the creator's wallet bought during the launch window.
ERC-8004: a standard for on-chain agent identities. At launch, a market can be bound to an agent id that the creator owns.
Agent id: an identity in the ERC-8004 registry of one chain. An id means nothing without its chain.
MCP: the Model Context Protocol. ADEXTO's MCP server lets an AI agent read markets and prepare launch, stake and claim transactions.
A2A: the Agent2Agent protocol. ADEXTO answers it at `/api/a2a` with the same launch and buy flows as MCP.
x402: a way to pay for an HTTP request. ADEXTO's gateway answers HTTP 402 with a USDC quote on Base, and delivers the token after you sign a payment.
EIP-3009: the USDC transfer authorization that an x402 buyer signs. It moves USDC without the buyer paying gas or granting an allowance.
Unsigned transaction: a transaction that ADEXTO builds and returns for your wallet or agent to sign and send. ADEXTO never holds your key for it.
Chain id: the number that identifies a network, such as 143 for Monad or 8453 for Base. Check it together with any address.
Factory: the contract that launches markets on a chain. Version 1.0.0 runs on all six chains, with byte-for-byte identical runtime code.
Indexer: a service that reads chain events into a database. ADEXTO uses Envio, subgraphs on The Graph and direct log scans, and any of them can lag behind the chain.
Stake hub: one staking contract per chain for markets launched by ADEXTO factories. It has no owner, no lock and no reward.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.lede: Short answers to the questions people ask most about launching and trading on ADEXTO.

sections.heading: Do I need to add liquidity to launch?

blocks.text: No. The launch transaction accepts no deposit, so you pay gas only. The curve starts from a virtual native reserve, and the whole supply goes into it at launch.

sections.heading: Does the creator get any tokens?

blocks.text: No. The creator receives no allocation. Instead, the creator earns a fixed part of every trade, 0.70% on the Standard tier, which accrues in the curve and is claimed from Creator earnings.

sections.heading: Can the fees change after launch?

blocks.text: No. Every fee rate and every payout address is written into the market when it is created, and nothing can change them later. There is no owner and no admin key on the launch path.

sections.heading: Does a market graduate to another exchange?

blocks.text: No. The curve never graduates or migrates; it stays the market's venue for its whole life. Anyone can still pair the token on another exchange, where the price can differ from the curve's.

sections.heading: Why is the same ticker on two chains?

blocks.text: Each chain is a separate market with its own curve, supply and price, and nothing is bridged between them. Check the chain on the market page before you trade.

sections.heading: Why did my buy fail in the first minutes of a market?

blocks.text: For the first 180 seconds, no wallet may hold more than 1% of the supply. A buy that would take a wallet past that reverts. Buy less, or wait for the window to end.

On the chain where your market launched, the factory reserves the ticker for good, in any letter case. The Studio and the agent launch tools also refuse a ticker that another creator already uses on a different chain.
No security firm has reviewed them. The output of automated analysers is published on the Security page, and bugs can be reported privately through GitHub.
You do. Trades go from your wallet straight to the curve, and ADEXTO never holds your key. A cross-chain swap is carried by the bridge named on the route you pick.
A stake at or above a market's minimum opens that market's agent to your address over MCP, and on markets that offer it, an Agent Compute key. It pays no reward, and nothing is locked.
No. Market data, leaderboards and the answers of a market's agent describe what happened on chain. They are not advice.

sections.heading: How do I report a scam market?

blocks.text: Use the Report page. A removed market disappears from ADEXTO's own site and tools; the contracts on chain are not touched.

studio-guide.title: Studio, step by step
studio-guide.lede: The Studio opens a market in one transaction. Express asks for a name, a ticker and an image; Advanced lets you set every option over five steps.

blocks.text: `/studio` opens in Express. Advanced is the five-step form at `/studio?mode=advanced`. Switching between them keeps what you typed, and both launch through the same factory call, simulated first.
Every launch goes to one chain. Each chain is its own market with its own supply and price, so to be on a second chain you launch there as well once the first market is live.
A link can fill the form in for someone else: `/studio?mode=express&name=…&symbol=…&chain=…`. The `Copy launch link` button builds one from what you typed.

items: Name: up to 64 characters.
Ticker: 2 to 12 letters or digits. It is permanent on the chain you launch on.
What is it? (optional): one line of up to 160 characters.
Image: upload one, generate one, or leave it out.
Chain: the one chain this market lives on.

blocks.text: The `Settings used` panel shows what Express fills in for you: the Standard fee of 1.00% per trade with 0.70% of it to you, and a supply of 1,000,000,000 tokens, all of them in the curve and none to you. To change any of it, switch to Advanced.

items: Chains: pick the chain to launch on.
Token: the name, the ticker, the supply (1,000,000,000 by default), a category, a description with links, and an image.
Curve: the fee tier. The opening market cap is about $4,000 on every chain.
Agent: an optional mandate for the market's agent, up to 1,000 characters, and an optional ERC-8004 agent id to bind.
Verify: review everything, sign the launch attestation, and launch.

blocks.text: Advanced offers three tiers. The 0.10% protocol part is inside each total.

items: Low, 0.60% per trade: 0.40% to the creator, 0.05% to the buyback, 0.05% to depth.
Standard, 1.00% (the default): 0.70% to the creator, 0.10% to the buyback, 0.10% to depth.
Meme, 2.00%: 1.50% to the creator, 0.20% to the buyback, 0.20% to depth.

blocks.text: The tier is written into the market at launch and can never be changed, by you or by anyone else.

items: Category: DeFi, AI agents, Meme, Gaming, Infrastructure, Real-world assets, Social or Other.
Description and links: a pitch of up to 160 characters, an X handle, a website, GitHub and docs. Links must start with http or https.
Image: PNG, JPEG or WebP, square, up to 2 MB, resized to 256×256. Ten robot presets are there if you have no image.

blocks.text: The description, links and image are kept by the ADEXTO site and are not part of the launch transaction. The launch metadata is anchored with an upload to 0G Storage that ADEXTO pays for, or with a keccak hash of the metadata when that upload fails. The anchor is a pointer to content, not an attestation.

Names, tickers and descriptions that impersonate or mislead are refused before anything is signed: for example ones built on words like official, airdrop, giveaway or claim, ones that use another brand's name or the ADEXTO name, and ones that carry malicious links or link shorteners.

Some tickers are reserved on every chain, such as ADEXTO, ETH, WETH, USDC, USDT, BTC, WBTC, 0G, MON and ARB. Robinhood Chain also reserves USDG and the tickers of listed stocks, and Arc reserves ARC, EURC, USYC and CIRBTC.

A ticker that already has a market on the chain you picked is taken, and so is a ticker that another creator uses on a different chain. Preparing a launch is limited to 6 tries per 10 minutes per IP address.

sections.heading: The cost card and the two wallet prompts

blocks.text: Before you launch, the cost card shows what the launch costs. There is no liquidity deposit, because the launch is not payable, and you receive no tokens, because the whole supply enters the curve. The gas figure is an estimate of about 3.3 million gas at the current gas price, and on Base it does not include the L1 data fee.

Your wallet then asks twice. First comes a free signature, the launch attestation, which states your address, the ticker, a timestamp and the version of the Terms and Acceptable Use Policy you accept. It is valid for 30 minutes. Then comes the launch transaction, which costs gas.
The attestation shows that an address signed. It is not a Sybil barrier: one person can still use many addresses.

items: A link to your market's page, and one to Creator earnings, where your fee share is tracked and claimed.
A launch kit: a share card, a button that adds the Telegram alert bot to your group, a link to the stake panel, and whether DEX Screener and GeckoTerminal list the market yet.
Announcement buttons that post to X or Farcaster, or copy the text.
The clean-launch proof, read from chain. Adding `&proof=1` to the market link opens it.

agent-launch.title: Launch from an agent
agent-launch.lede: An agent can launch a market through ADEXTO's MCP server, its REST routes or A2A. ADEXTO prepares the transaction, and the agent signs and sends it with its own key.

items: An MCP client pointed at `https://adexto.xyz/api/mcp`, or any HTTP client for the REST and A2A routes.
A key that the agent controls, with gas on the chain it launches on.
A name and a ticker. Agent launches use fixed settings: 1.00% per trade, of which 0.70% goes to the creator and 0.10% is the protocol part, and a supply of 1,000,000,000.

blocks.code: claude mcp add --transport http adexto https://adexto.xyz/api/mcp

blocks.text: The `/agents` page has the same setup for Claude Code, Cursor, A2A and OpenAI Agents, with a `Copy MCP URL` button.

items: Call `prepare_launch` with `chainId`, `name`, `symbol` and `deployer`, and optionally `agentId`, a description, links, an image and a category. It checks the chain, the ticker and the agent id, and returns an attestation message that stays valid for 1,800 seconds.
Sign that message with the deployer key. It is a free EIP-191 signature that moves nothing.

Call `prepare_launch` again with the same arguments plus `attestationMessage` and `attestationSignature`. It anchors the metadata and returns an unsigned transaction: `from`, `to` (the factory), `data`, a `value` of 0, `chainId` and `gas`.
Sign and send that transaction from the deployer address.

Call `register_launch` with the chain id and the transaction hash. It reads the factory's event from the receipt and lists the market on the site, in `list_markets` and on the x402 gateway. It is safe to call twice.

blocks.text: The gas limit includes a margin: 5% on Monad, which charges for the gas limit rather than the gas used, and 20% on the other chains.

The same flow works without MCP. `/api/agents/launch/preflight` runs the first step only: it checks a launch and returns the attestation message, and it never signs, anchors or sends anything. `/api/agents/launch/prepare` and `/api/agents/launch/register` are the second step and the registration. The routes allow 30 requests per 5 minutes.
The launch console on `/agents` (`Check before launch`) calls the preflight, so you can see whether a name, a ticker and a chain would pass before an agent signs anything.

An A2A client sends a data part with `{"skill":"launch_market","chainId":143,"name":"…","symbol":"…","deployer":"0x…"}` to `/api/a2a`. The task asks for the attestation signature, then returns the unsigned transaction, and completes when it receives the `txHash`.

Pass `agentId` to bind the new market to an ERC-8004 agent. The factory checks that the deployer owns that id on that chain's registry, so register the agent first, from the same wallet, at `/agents/identity`.

market-page.title: The market page
market-page.lede: Every market has a page with its price, chart, trades, holders, your position and a swap card.

blocks.text: The header shows the name, the ticker and badges. `Contract verified on-chain` means the token contract was confirmed on chain when the market was registered. A market without it is marked as a showcase entry, which was not minted by an ADEXTO factory. A market bound to an agent also shows its ERC-8004 badge.

Links open the token on the chain's explorer, the curve (`Pool`) and the market's x402 API. Share buttons post the market to X, Telegram, WhatsApp or Reddit, or make an image card of the market or of your own position.
The figures are per chain: the market cap, the price in USD, the supply and the price in the chain's own asset. The same ticker on another chain has its own figures.

items: Unit: USD, the default, or the chain's own asset.
Style: candles or a line. View: price or MCAP, which is the fully diluted value, because the whole supply started in the curve.
Timeframes: 1m (the default), 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h and 1d, plus 1s, 5s and 15s in the native unit. `All` shows the whole history since launch, in at most 160 bars.
Indicators: EMA 9, EMA 21, SMA 50, Bollinger Bands (20, 2) and VWAP on the price, and RSI 14 and MACD (12, 26, 9) in a pane of their own. The price axis can be logarithmic or automatic.
Time: shown in your own time zone. Daily candles are fixed UTC days.

blocks.text: Candles are built from every trade since launch. USD candles use the native/USD rates that ADEXTO has recorded; where no rate was recorded for a period, the chart says so instead of filling in today's rate.
`Curve depth ladder` shows how far the price would move for buys and sells of different sizes. It is computed from the curve's reserves, so it is not an order book: nobody has placed those orders.
The trade feed shows all trades, only yours (`Mine`), only the creator's (`Dev`), or only the large ones (`Large`), which move at least 1% of the supply. Trades are marked BUY, SELL or AUTO_BUYBACK.
`Holders` shows the number of holders, the share of the top 10, the creator's share and the share still in the curve, rebuilt from every transfer since the token was minted.

With a wallet connected, the position panel shows your balance, your average entry, your cost basis, unrealized and realized profit and loss, and `Exit value`, what selling your balance would return now. All of it comes from your own trades on chain.
The creator's wallet also sees its fee earnings above the swap card, with a button to claim them.

items: `Max slippage`: 0.5%, 1% (the default), 3% or 5%. The deadline is fixed at 600 seconds.
The 25%, 50%, 75% and Max buttons keep a little of the chain's own asset back for gas.
`Minimum received` and `Price impact` are shown before you sign, with the fee split into curve depth, creator, agent buyback and protocol.
A sale approves the exact amount, then sells (`Approve & sell`).
Every trade is simulated before your wallet opens, so a trade that would revert is caught before you pay gas for it.

blocks.text: `Not enough MON`, or the chain's own asset, means the wallet cannot cover the amount plus gas. `More than the curve holds` means the buy asks for more tokens than the curve has left.

On a phone the page has three tabs. `Trade` has the chart and the swap card. `Market` has the 24-hour volume, traders and transactions, the same ticker on other chains, the depth ladder and trades, the holders, and the market's agent. `You` has your position, the stake panel and the launch facts.

finding-markets.title: Finding markets
finding-markets.lede: The Explorer lists every market on every chain, and the Leaderboard shows which ones people are actually buying.

blocks.text: `/explorer` lists the markets that ADEXTO knows about, and its header counts how many have a bonding curve you can trade.

items: Search by ticker, name or address.
Filter by chain, by category, or to your watchlist.
Sort by `Largest` or `Newest`.
Each row shows the chain, a `verified` or `showcase` badge, and whether its curve is live. `Terminal` opens the market page, and `Swap` opens the swap.

blocks.text: A market that was removed after a report shows `Removed from this site`. Removal only affects ADEXTO's own site and tools; the contracts keep running on chain.

The star next to a market's name adds it to your watchlist, and the `Watchlist` chip in the Explorer shows only those markets. The list is kept in this browser's local storage, so it does not follow you to another device or browser.
`/leaderboard` shows who is actually buying, in five lists:

items: Trending: markets ranked by the number of different wallets that bought in the last 24 hours.
Newest launches.
Top creators.
Agent-bound markets: the ones bound to an ERC-8004 agent.
Launch of the week. There is no prize.

blocks.text: ADEXTO team wallets and each market's own creator are left out of the counts, so a creator's own buys do not move their market up.

sections.heading: The same ticker on several chains

blocks.text: A ticker can have markets on several chains, each with its own curve, supply and price. The Explorer shows the chain on every row, and a market page lists the same ticker's other chains under `Independent pool and price per chain · no bridging`.

cross-chain.title: Cross-chain swaps
cross-chain.lede: The Cross-chain tab on `/swap` moves value between chains through LI.FI. You sign in your own wallet, and a bridge carries the funds.

blocks.text: Open `/swap` and choose `Cross-chain`. Pick what you send and what you want to receive on the other chain. ADEXTO asks LI.FI for routes from its server, and you sign the route you pick in your own wallet.
Routes are found by LI.FI and carried by the bridge named on each route. ADEXTO never holds the funds, and no integrator fee is set on these routes.
The funds arrive at the same address that sent them. There is no field for another recipient.

items: Monad: MON and USDC.
Arbitrum One: ETH, USDC and USDG.
Robinhood Chain: ETH and USDG.
Base: ETH and USDC.

blocks.text: Arc is not in the Cross-chain tab. Market tokens are not bridged either: a token bought on one chain stays a token of that chain's market.

items: Route preference: `Most received` or `Fastest delivery`.
Slippage: 0.3%, 0.5% (the default), 1% or 3%.
Bridges: allow or deny particular bridges.

blocks.text: Only single-step routes are offered, so a transfer is one transaction on the sending chain, after an approval when the token needs one. If a route would lose more than 10% of the value, the tab warns you before you sign.
Each route states a minimum: at least that amount arrives, or the bridge refunds you. How long a transfer takes depends on the bridge.

wallets.title: Wallets and networks
wallets.lede: ADEXTO works with browser wallets and WalletConnect. Your wallet signs everything, and ADEXTO never asks for your seed phrase.

blocks.text: `Choose wallet` lists the wallets installed in your browser, found through EIP-6963, and offers WalletConnect for mobile and desktop wallets that connect with a QR code.
ADEXTO never asks for a seed phrase or a private key. Anyone who does, in a direct message or on a page that looks like ADEXTO, is not ADEXTO.

Every market lives on one chain. When you trade, the app asks your wallet to switch to that chain, and to add it if the wallet does not have it yet. If you decline, trading stays blocked until the wallet is on the right network.

On Robinhood Chain, the network that the app adds to your wallet uses ADEXTO's public RPC at `https://adexto.xyz/api/public-rpc/robinhood`. It allows 240 requests per minute per IP address and 20 raw transactions per 5 minutes. A wallet that added the network earlier keeps its own RPC, because adding a network never overwrites one that exists.

items: Monad: MON. Monad charges for the gas limit rather than the gas used.
Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain and Base: ETH. On Base, an L1 data fee is added to the L2 gas.
Arc: USDC, which is Arc's own gas asset.
Check the network and the contract in the wallet prompt before you confirm.
A sale asks for an approval of the exact amount, not an unlimited allowance.
The messages that ADEXTO asks you to sign, such as the launch attestation or the Agent Compute key message, move nothing and cost nothing.
An x402 payment is also a signature, but it authorizes a USDC transfer. Read the amount before you sign it.

creator-earnings.title: Creator earnings
creator-earnings.lede: A creator holds no tokens and earns a fixed part of every trade instead. It accrues in the curve and is claimed at `/creator`.

blocks.text: Every trade pays the market's fee, and the creator's part was fixed at launch: 0.70% of each trade on the Standard tier, 0.40% on Low and 1.50% on Meme. It accrues inside the curve, in the chain's own asset, until it is claimed.
The payout address was fixed in the curve when the market was created. Anyone can send the claim transaction, and the money always goes to that address.
`/creator` shows `Earned, all time`, `Claimable now` and the number of markets, for your connected wallet or for any address in the link, as in `/creator?address=0x…`.
`Claim` appears for your own wallet only. With several markets on one chain, `Claim all` collects every one of them in a single transaction through Multicall3.
A claim costs gas. When little has accrued, the gas can cost more than the claim pays, so it can make sense to wait.
The MCP tool `prepare_claim` returns unsigned claim transactions for an address on a chain: one `claimCreatorFees()` call per curve, or one Multicall3 batch when several curves owe fees.
The same figures are public at `/api/creator/earnings?address=0x…`, limited to 30 requests per minute.

sections.heading: On the market page and in Telegram

blocks.text: On a market page, the creator's wallet sees its earnings above the swap card. In Telegram, `/earnings <address>` asks the ADEXTO bot what an address has earned.

staking.title: Staking
staking.lede: Staking a market's token opens that market's agent to you over MCP and, where offered, an Agent Compute key. There is no lock and no reward.

blocks.text: A stake at or above the market's minimum is active. An active stake opens the market's agent to your address over MCP (`ask_agent`), and on markets that offer it, an Agent Compute key.
Staking pays no reward and is not a yield. Nothing is locked: you can unstake at any time.

Each chain has one stake hub, which accepts tokens launched by ADEXTO factories. Its minimum is 1/100,000 of the token's supply, which is 10,000 tokens for a supply of 1,000,000,000. The hub has no owner.
A few markets have a stake contract of their own instead: $ADEXTO on 0G, with a minimum of 5,000, and $SAI on Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain and Monad, with a minimum of 10,000 on each.
The stake panel on the market page shows the total staked, the number of stakers, the minimum and your own stake.

items: Open the market page and find `Stake`. On a phone it is in the `You` tab.
Enter an amount at or above the minimum and press Stake. The wallet asks for an approval of the exact amount if needed, then for the stake.
To leave, press `Unstake all`. A partial unstake has to leave either nothing or at least the minimum.

blocks.text: An agent can do the same with `prepare_stake`, which checks the balance, the minimum and whether the hub accepts the token, and returns unsigned transactions. `check_stake` reads a stake.

items: Call `access_message` for the market and your address, and sign the message it returns. Signing moves nothing and costs nothing.
Within 10 minutes, call `ask_agent` with the signature and your question.

blocks.text: The answer comes from glm-5.3 on the 0G router and is limited to facts read on chain for that call, which the tool returns next to the answer. Without an active stake it is refused, and nothing is charged either way. It is not advice.

compute.title: Agent Compute
compute.lede: Stake a token and get your own API key for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that serves DeepSeek-V4-Flash through 0G Compute. It is a beta.

blocks.text: Agent Compute turns a stake into an API key. The key calls `0g/deepseek-v4-flash` at `https://compute.adexto.xyz/v1`, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint served by 0G Compute. The model accepts a context of 1,441,792 tokens and can return up to 393,216.
The 0G router reports that the model runs in a TDX trusted execution environment. ADEXTO shows that report and does not verify the underlying quote itself.
Usage is counted in tokens, input plus output, from the router's records, and adds up from the day the key is created.
A stake in $ADEXTO on 0G, or in $SAI on Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain or Monad, opens a tier by its size:

items: Starter: an allowance of 100,000 tokens, about 121 requests, for 5,000 ADEXTO or 10,000 SAI.
Builder: 300,000 tokens, about 364 requests, for 25,000 ADEXTO or 50,000 SAI.
Operator: 600,000 tokens, about 729 requests, for 100,000 ADEXTO or 250,000 SAI.
Sovereign: 1,000,000 tokens, about 1,215 requests, for 250,000 ADEXTO or 1,000,000 SAI.

blocks.text: The request counts assume the roughly 823 input tokens that the router adds to every call. Longer prompts and answers use more. When the allowance is spent, raising the stake opens a larger one.

Any other market launched on ADEXTO can be staked in its chain's stake hub, and its keys are funded by that market's own trading. Half of the 0.10% protocol part that the curve collects is valued in USD at the current native price and turned into model tokens at $0.3168 per million.

That allowance is shared among the market's keys in proportion to each key's stake, and only fees that arrive after a key exists count toward it. A key stays on while at least 823 tokens of allowance remain, which takes about $0.52 of trading per request.
A market with no trading funds no compute. Launching a token and staking it yourself gives nothing until other people trade it.

items: Stake the token at or above its minimum.
On `/agent-compute`, choose the token and sign a message with the staking address. Signing moves nothing.
Copy the key. It is shown once; if you lose it, revoke it and issue a new one.

blocks.text: Each address gets one key per token, and at most 5 keys can be issued per hour from one IP address. A key can be revoked at any time.
Send `"stream": false` unless your client reads server-sent events. Without it, the router answers as an event stream.

items: The allowances are a policy, not a right that a contract guarantees.
Usage is checked on a schedule, so a key can go slightly past its allowance before it is switched off.
A key is switched off when its stake falls below the minimum, when its allowance is spent, or when its market is no longer listed.

referrals.title: Referrals
referrals.lede: Share a referral link and earn 25% of the 0.10% protocol part on the trades you bring, paid weekly by the ADEXTO team.

blocks.text: Your link is any ADEXTO page with `?ref=` and your code. The code is a handle of 3 to 20 characters, using lowercase letters, digits and underscores, or your wallet address.

When someone opens your link and agrees to it, the code is kept in their browser for 30 days. Trades they then send from the ADEXTO site carry your address at the end of the transaction data, after an `ADXR` marker, which the curve ignores.
You earn 25% of the 0.10% protocol part on the volume you refer, which is 0.025% of that volume. Rewards are counted weekly, from Monday to Monday UTC, and paid for each week whose reward reaches $5.
Payouts are made by the ADEXTO team and reviewed by hand. No token is promised, and referral totals are not points that can be transferred or traded.

items: One level only: you are credited for the wallets you bring, not for the wallets they bring.
You cannot refer yourself. A trade whose buyer, seller or recipient is your own address does not count.
ADEXTO team wallets can neither refer nor be referred.
Patterns that look like one person trading through many wallets to farm credit are excluded.
Only trades sent from the ADEXTO site with your code attached carry the referral.

blocks.text: `/rewards` shows your link, the trades you have referred so far, and the totals of the whole program.

a2a.title: A2A
a2a.lede: ADEXTO answers the Agent2Agent protocol at `/api/a2a`: launch a market, buy with x402, or read markets, using JSON data parts.

blocks.text: The card is at `https://adexto.xyz/.well-known/agent-card.json`. It names the agent `ADEXTO Launchpad` and lists four skills: `launch_market`, `buy_token`, `list_markets` and `get_market`.

The endpoint speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP. Send the header `A2A-Version: 1.0` to use version 1.0; without it, the server answers in the version 0.3 format, and it accepts the method names of both. The version 1.0 methods are `SendMessage`, `GetTask`, `CancelTask` and `ListTasks`.
There is no streaming and no push notification. The agent does not run a language model: it works from JSON data parts, and free text gets an answer that explains how to use the skills.
`list_markets` and `get_market` answer at once with a message, without a task.

items: Send a data part with `skill` set to `launch_market`, plus `chainId`, `name`, `symbol` and `deployer`, and optionally `agentId` and `description`. The task asks for input and returns an `attestationMessage`.
Sign it with the deployer key and send `attestationSignature` in the same task. The task returns the unsigned launch transaction.
Sign and send the transaction yourself, then send its `txHash`. The task registers the market and completes.

blocks.text: Tasks are kept in memory for up to 6 hours. If a task is lost after the transaction was sent, send the `txHash` in a new task, or call `register_launch` over MCP.

`buy_token` is a two-turn task on the a2a-x402 extension, version 0.2. Send a data part with `skill` set to `buy_token`, plus `symbol`, `chainId` and `to`. The task returns the gateway's payment requirements; you sign the EIP-3009 payment and send it back in the same task. ADEXTO's A2A server signs nothing for you.

Each IP address can send 60 messages and 300 reads per 5 minutes. There is no authentication: a task id is random and works as the key to its task, so anyone who has the id can read or cancel the task. `ListTasks` only returns the tasks in a `contextId` you give it.

public-api.title: Public API
public-api.lede: Read-only HTTP endpoints for markets, prices, holders and launch facts, plus contract ABIs and discovery files for agents. No key is needed.

items: Every endpoint on this page is public and read-only, and answers in JSON unless it serves an image.
Rate limits are kept per server process. A limit per IP address answers 429; a shared limit answers 503.
Figures come from chain reads and from ADEXTO's indexes, which can trail a brand-new market or trade for a moment.

`GET /api/graphql`: the market list that the site itself uses, with prices in each chain's own asset and the `verified` and `poolLive` flags. Despite the path, it is not a GraphQL server: it returns the whole list and ignores any query.
`GET /api/pool?symbol=&chainId=`: one market's curve, reserves and spot price, or `tradable: false` with a reason.
`GET /api/prices`: the USD prices of the native assets, with a `live` flag that says whether the price feeds answered.
`GET /api/fx-history?symbol=`: the native/USD rates that ADEXTO has recorded, which the chart uses for USD candles.
`GET /api/agent/telemetry?symbol=&chainId=`: a market's trade history, up to 5,000 trades, with candles built from all of it.
`GET /api/leaderboard`: the data behind `/leaderboard`.

`GET /api/market/holders?symbol=&chainId=`: the holder count and the shares of the top 10, the creator and the curve, rebuilt from every transfer since mint. `complete: false` means the first scan has not finished yet.
`GET /api/market/position?symbol=&chainId=&wallet=`: one wallet's balance, average entry, cost basis and profit and loss in one market.
`GET /api/creator/earnings?address=`: what an address has earned and can claim as a creator.

blocks.text: The holder and position endpoints allow 60 requests per 5 minutes, and creator earnings 30 per minute.

items: `GET /api/launch-cost`: what opening a market costs on each chain now, from the measured gas, the current gas price and the native price. A chain whose RPC does not answer is reported with `live: false`.
`GET /api/launch-proof?chainId=&token=`: the clean-launch proof of one market, read from chain. `token` is an address or the market's slug.

`GET /api/deploy`: the factory on each chain, with its version and protocol fee read from chain. With `?symbol=`, and optionally `chainIds=`, it says whether a ticker is still free in ADEXTO's registry.
`GET /api/listing-status?chainId=&token=`: whether DEX Screener and GeckoTerminal show the market yet.
`GET /api/tee`: the attestation status that the 0G router reports for the agent models. `live: false` means the router could not be reached, which is not the same as safe.
`/api/share-card/<token>?chain=`: a 1200×630 share image of a market. The `/position` and `/launch-proof` paths under it make the position and proof cards.
`/abi/AdextoFactory.json`, `/abi/AdextoCurve.json` and `/abi/AdextoToken.json`, listed in `/abi/index.json`: the contract ABIs.
`/.well-known/agent-card.json` for A2A, `/.well-known/agent-registration.json`, and `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` for MCP: discovery files for agents.
`/api/dexscreener` and `/api/dextools`: the adapters that DEX Screener and DEXTools read.

blocks.text: `POST /api/indexer/graphql` is a read-only GraphQL proxy to ADEXTO's Envio indexer for Monad, Robinhood Chain and Arc. It allows 60 queries per minute, each up to 16,000 bytes, and can be called from a browser. Entity ids look like `<chainId>_<address>`.

blocks.code:
curl -s https://adexto.xyz/api/indexer/graphql \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"{ Swap(limit: 5, order_by: {timestamp: desc}, where: {chainId: {_eq: 143}}) { txHash isBuy amountIn amountOut timestamp } }"}'

blocks.text: Base and Arbitrum One are indexed by subgraphs on The Graph, at `https://api.studio.thegraph.com/query/1757874/adexto-base/v1.0.1` and the same path with `adexto-arbitrum`. Their entities include `Project`, `Curve`, `Swap`, `BuybackBurn` and `CreatorFeeClaim`. These are development endpoints, and The Graph limits how much they can be queried.

telegram.title: Telegram bot
telegram.lede: The ADEXTO bot posts new launches and buys, answers questions about a market, and can post every buy of a market in your own group.

items: `/market <ticker> [chain]`: the price, buyers, holders and creator fees of a market, with links.
`/launch [TICKER] [name]`: a Studio link with your token filled in. You still sign the launch in your own wallet.
`/earnings <address>`: what a creator address has earned.
`/alerts`: in a group, post every buy of a market there. Only group admins can change it.

blocks.text: The bot is at `https://t.me/Adextofeedbot`.

items: Add the bot to your group. The `Add the alert bot` button in the Studio's launch kit opens Telegram with your market already chosen.
As a group admin, send `/alerts <ticker> [chain]`. A group can follow up to 10 markets.
Send `/alerts` on its own to see what the group follows, `/alerts off <ticker>` to stop one market, and `/alerts off` to stop them all.

blocks.text: The ADEXTO Telegram at `https://t.me/adexto` gets every new launch and every buy worth at least $1. Sells are not posted, and neither are buys by ADEXTO team wallets.

A buy made through x402 is shown under the wallet that received the tokens, not the relayer that sent the transaction. When the feed first sees a market, it starts from that market's newest trade, so old history is not replayed.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.lede: What the common errors mean, and what to do about each of them.

sections.heading: A buy or a sale fails

items: `Anti-sniper: wallet limit during launch window`: for the first 180 seconds of a market, no wallet may hold more than 1% of the supply. Buy less, or wait until the window ends.
`AdextoCurve: slippage`: the price moved past your `Max slippage` before the trade was mined. Try again, or raise the limit if you accept a worse price.
`AdextoCurve: expired`: the trade waited past its 600-second deadline. Send it again.
`More than the curve holds`, or `AdextoCurve: insufficient curve liquidity`: the buy asks for more tokens than the curve has left. Buy less.
`Not enough MON`, or ETH, USDC or 0G: the wallet cannot cover the amount plus gas. The Max button keeps some back for gas.
`Rejected in wallet.`: you declined the prompt, and nothing was sent.

sections.heading: The wallet is on the wrong network

blocks.text: The app asks the wallet to switch to the market's chain, and to add it if needed. If you decline, trading stays blocked; switch the network in the wallet and try again.

On Robinhood Chain, a wallet that added the network earlier keeps its own RPC. If transactions never reach the chain, point the network's RPC in your wallet at `https://adexto.xyz/api/public-rpc/robinhood`.

items: The ticker is taken: it has a market on that chain already, another creator uses it on a different chain, or it is reserved. Pick another ticker.
Too many tries: preparing a launch is limited to 6 tries per 10 minutes per IP address. Wait, then try again.
The attestation expired: a signed attestation is valid for 30 minutes. Start the launch again to get a fresh message.
The gas is higher than the estimate: the cost card estimates about 3.3 million gas, and on Base the L1 data fee comes on top.

blocks.text: If the launch transaction was mined but the market does not appear, it has not been registered yet. `register_launch`, over MCP or at `/api/agents/launch/register`, registers it from the chain id and the transaction hash, and it is safe to repeat.

sections.heading: A market or a trade is missing

blocks.text: Indexers can trail the chain, so a new market or a fresh trade can take a moment to appear in lists and charts. The chain has the trade as soon as it is mined: look it up on the chain's explorer.
Holder figures say so when the first scan of a market has not finished, and the chart says so when no USD rate was recorded for a period.

sections.heading: A claim or a buyback fails

items: `AdextoCurve: nothing to claim`: no fees have accrued since the last claim.
`AdextoCurve: buyback cooldown`: a buyback ran less than an hour ago, and each curve allows one per hour.
A claim worth less than its gas is not an error, but it can be worth waiting until more has accrued.

blocks.text: 429 means your IP address reached a rate limit: wait, then retry. 503 means a shared limit or an upstream service is busy. The x402 gateway answers 503 before it takes any payment when it cannot fill an order.
Ask in the ADEXTO Telegram at `https://t.me/adexto`, or open an issue at `https://github.com/0xcuy/adexto/issues`. Never share your seed phrase or private key with anyone who offers to help.

check-a-market.title: Check a market
check-a-market.lede: Before you buy, you can check how a market was launched, who created it and where its supply is, all from chain.

blocks.text: A market page has a `Clean launch` panel, read from chain through `/api/launch-proof`. Adding `&proof=1` to a market link opens it. It covers markets from the current 1.0.0 factories and the earlier 0.11.0 ones; for anything else it makes no claim at all.

items: The creator's balance right after the launch transaction, from the transfers in its receipt.
That the whole supply went into the curve and the factory kept none.
That the factory is ADEXTO's known factory for that chain, with a matching version, and that the token and the curve point at each other.
The launch window and its cap, and the fee split, from the contracts themselves.
That the token, the curve and the factory have no owner, and that none of them is a proxy.
Whether the creator's wallet bought during the launch window.

blocks.text: A creator who buys from another wallet cannot be seen by any check, and the proof does not claim otherwise.

`Contract verified on-chain` means the token contract was confirmed on chain when the market was registered. A `showcase` entry was not minted by an ADEXTO factory, so the factory's rules on fees, supply and owners do not apply to it.
The explorer and `Pool` links open the token and the curve on the chain's explorer. Compare those addresses, and the factory that created them, with the list under Contracts and status.
`Holders` shows the share of the top 10 wallets, the creator's share and what is still in the curve. The trade feed's `Dev` filter shows the creator's own trades.

A market bound to an ERC-8004 agent shows the agent's badge, which links to its public card at `/agents/id/<chainId>/<agentId>`. The binding proves that the creator owned that agent id on that chain when the market launched. It says nothing about what the agent does or how well.

sections.heading: What no check can tell you

items: Whether the project behind a token is real, or whether its links belong to who they claim. The Studio refuses obvious impersonation, but it cannot check identities.
Whether the creator also holds the token through other wallets.
What the price will do.

risks.title: Risks
risks.lede: What can go wrong when you launch or trade on ADEXTO, in plain words.

blocks.text: A bonding curve moves the price with every trade. Early buyers pay less and later buyers pay more, and every sale pushes the price back down toward where the market opened. A buyer can lose most of what they paid.
Nothing on ADEXTO is financial advice: not the market data, not the leaderboard, and not the answers of a market's agent.

No security firm has reviewed the contracts. Automated analysers have run, and their output is published, but that does not rule out a bug. There is no proxy and no upgrade path, so a bug in a market that already exists cannot be fixed in place.

Each market depends on its chain, and a chain can halt, reorganize or change its fees. A cross-chain swap depends on the bridge named on the route: if a transfer fails, that bridge's refund rules apply.

An x402 purchase is two steps on two chains and is not atomic: the operator delivers the tokens first and collects your USDC second. `pay_and_buy` signs with the operator's key, within fixed limits, so the funds it spends are the operator's, not yours.

Anyone can launch a market, and a name or an image can imitate a real project. The Studio refuses obvious cases, and reported markets are removed from ADEXTO's own site and tools, but the contracts keep running on chain. Check the creator, the chain and the address before you buy.
ADEXTO never asks for your seed phrase or private key.

The same address can exist on several chains with different contents, so funds sent to the right address on the wrong chain can be lost. Sending a chain's own asset straight to a curve address buys tokens with no slippage limit; use the swap card, or a call with a minimum output, instead.

The site, the indexers, the MCP and A2A servers, the Telegram bot and the x402 gateway are run by ADEXTO and can be slow or down. The contracts do not depend on them: a curve can always be traded by calling it directly.
Agent Compute is a beta, and its allowances are a policy, not a right that a contract guarantees.

reporting.title: Report a market
reporting.lede: If a market impersonates someone, links to malware or breaks the Acceptable Use Policy, report it. Removal takes it off ADEXTO's site and tools; the chain is untouched.

blocks.text: Open `/report`. It links to a GitHub issue form for market reports and to the ADEXTO Telegram. Include the chain, the ticker or the token address, and what is wrong.
To report a security bug in the contracts or the site, use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting instead, so the details are not public before a fix.
A removed market disappears from the ADEXTO site, the x402 gateway, MCP and A2A, the Telegram bot and the aggregator feeds. Its page shows `Removed from this site`.
Removal does not touch the chain. The token and its curve keep working for anyone who calls them directly, and the ticker stays taken on that chain.

The Terms and the Acceptable Use Policy, version 2026-10-05, set out what may be launched. The Studio already refuses names and links that impersonate a brand or ADEXTO, promise airdrops or giveaways, or point to malicious sites and link shorteners.
